precepts.text: They that are delivered shall rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord in the places of drawing water; that duty stands even before all twelve tribes are gathered.
precepts.point: All twelve tribes are not gathered together right now, but we are still commanded to rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord, and that takes gathering; the body must move in one unison, in one direction, as a camp.

note.label: Numbers 4: The Service of the Tabernacle Done in Order

precepts.why:
The Lord referred to all the tribes together as the camp: the sons of Kohath came to bear the sanctuary “as the camp is to set forward.” If you are not in a camp you are out of order. People avoid camps because a camp carries a certain level of order and subjection, and they want to do their own thing, which is to sit in the midst of sin.

All twelve tribes are not gathered together right now, but the duty stands: “They that are delivered from the noise of archers in the places of drawing water, there shall they rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord, even the righteous acts toward the inhabitants of his villages in Israel: then shall the people of the Lord go down to the gates.”

We are still commanded to rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord, and that takes gathering. That duty stands even before all twelve tribes are gathered.

precepts.text: Speak the same thing, no divisions, perfectly joined together in the same mind and the same judgment; that is the camp moving in one direction.
precepts.point: All twelve tribes are not gathered together right now, but we are still commanded to rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord, and that takes gathering; the body must move in one unison, in one direction, as a camp.

note.label: Numbers 4: The Service of the Tabernacle Done in Order

precepts.why:
A camp moves in one unison, in one direction. “Now I beseech you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you; but that ye be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment.”

Speak the same thing, no divisions, perfectly joined together in the same mind and the same judgment: that is the body moving as a camp. The Most High is very particular about the most holy things, and the order of the camp is how the body moves in one direction.

precepts.text: Zacharias of the course of Abia was righteous, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless, and his lot was to burn incense in the temple; he served in the Kohathite charge.
precepts.point: The son of Zacharias was John the Baptist, a Levite; and John the Baptist was Elijah back on the earth again, come to do what was prophesied of him. There is no reincarnation, coming back as a bird or such; there is regeneration, and we come back over and over again.

note.label: Numbers 4: The Service of the Tabernacle Done in Order

precepts.why:
To the office of Eleazar pertained “the oil for the light, and the sweet incense, and the daily meat offering, and the anointing oil, and the oversight of all the tabernacle.” The burning of the sweet incense stayed in that priestly line. “There was in the days of Herod, the king of Judea, a certain priest named Zacharias, of the course of Abia: and his wife was of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elisabeth.” Zacharias descended from the line of the Kohathites.

“And they were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless.” That is the New Testament precept for what it means to be righteous: walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless. Highlight that and commit it to memory.

“And it came to pass, that while he executed the priest’s office before God in the order of his course, According to the custom of the priest’s office, his lot was to burn incense when he went into the temple of the Lord.” The sweet incense of Eleazar’s office was still being burned by his line in the temple in the days of Herod.

precepts.text: Elias is come already, and they knew him not; the disciples understood that he spake unto them of John the Baptist.
precepts.point: The son of Zacharias was John the Baptist, a Levite; and John the Baptist was Elijah back on the earth again, come to do what was prophesied of him. There is no reincarnation, coming back as a bird or such; there is regeneration, and we come back over and over again.

note.label: Numbers 4: The Service of the Tabernacle Done in Order

precepts.why:
The son of Zacharias was John the Baptist, a Levite of that priestly line. And John the Baptist was Elijah back on the earth again, come to do what was prophesied of him. “But I say unto you, That Elias is come already, and they knew him not, but have done unto him whatsoever they listed. Likewise shall also the Son of man suffer of them. Then the disciples understood that he spake unto them of John the Baptist.”

There is no reincarnation, coming back as a bird or such; there is regeneration, and we come back over and over again. Elias came already as John the Baptist, and they knew him not.

precepts.text: The service of the sons of Kohath is about the most holy things; Aaron and his sons take down the covering vail and cover the ark before the camp sets forward.
precepts.point: The Kohathites were in charge of carrying the sanctuary to and fro, and the reading further on shows them doing it once the camp moved.

note.label: Numbers 7: The Offering of the Princes at the Dedication of the Altar

precepts.why:
Gershon got two wagons and four oxen and Merari four wagons and eight oxen, “But unto the sons of Kohath he gave none: because the service of the sanctuary belonging unto them was that they should bear upon their shoulders.” Numbers 4 shows what that bearing was.

“This shall be the service of the sons of Kohath in the tabernacle of the congregation, about the most holy things: And when the camp setteth forward, Aaron shall come, and his sons, and they shall take down the covering vail, and cover the ark of testimony with it: And shall put thereon the covering of badgers’ skins, and shall spread over it a cloth wholly of blue, and shall put in the staves thereof.”

The service of the sons of Kohath is about the most holy things. Aaron and his sons covered the ark and the vessels first, and the staves were put in, because those things were carried on shoulders, not on wagons.

precepts.text: When Aaron has made an end of covering the sanctuary, the sons of Kohath come to bear it, but they shall not touch any holy thing, lest they die.
precepts.point: The Kohathites were in charge of carrying the sanctuary to and fro, and the reading further on shows them doing it once the camp moved.

note.label: Numbers 7: The Offering of the Princes at the Dedication of the Altar

precepts.why:
“And when Aaron and his sons have made an end of covering the sanctuary, and all the vessels of the sanctuary, as the camp is to set forward; after that, the sons of Kohath shall come to bear it: but they shall not touch any holy thing, lest they die. These things are the burden of the sons of Kohath in the tabernacle of the congregation.”

That is why the sons of Kohath received no wagons and no oxen. Their burden was the sanctuary itself, borne on their shoulders once Aaron had covered it, and not touching any holy thing lest they die. The Kohathites were in charge of carrying the sanctuary to and fro, and the reading further on shows them doing it once the camp moved.

precepts.text: The sons of Kohath were forbidden to touch the holy things lest they die; only the Levites bore the ark.
precepts.point: The anger of the Most High was kindled against Uzza, and He smote him because he put his hand to the ark, and he died there before the Most High. The ark was only to be touched by the Levites; the Most High does not play.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 13: Bringing Up the Ark

precepts.why:
When Aaron and his sons had covered the sanctuary and its vessels, “the sons of Kohath shall come to bear it: but they shall not touch any holy thing, lest they die.” The holy things were not to be handled; only the Levites bore the ark.

So when “the oxen stumbled”, and “Uzza put forth his hand to hold the ark”, “the anger of the Lord was kindled against Uzza, and he smote him, because he put his hand to the ark: and there he died before God.” The ark was only to be touched by the Levites. The Most High does not play.

moments.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: From thirty years old and upward even until fifty years old, all that enter into the host, to do the work in the tabernacle of the congregation.

So how come in Numbers 4 it says thirty, and in Numbers 8 it says twenty-five? From twenty-five to thirty they were learning — from who? From the elders that stopped doing the service, who were fifty and up. They were teaching them from the age of twenty-five to thirty. At thirty they entered in to do the service.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: The sons of Kohath were numbered from thirty years old and upward even unto fifty years old, all that enter into the host to do the work in the tabernacle of the congregation. You took on that responsibility at thirty years old.

note.label: Numbers 4: The Service of the Tabernacle Done in Order

points: This is the service of the sons of Kohath about the most holy things. When the camp set forward, Aaron and his sons took down the covering vail and covered the ark of the testimony with it, with the covering of badgers' skins and a cloth wholly of blue.

note.label: Numbers 4: The Service of the Tabernacle Done in Order

points: The table of shewbread, the candlestick, the golden altar, and all the instruments of ministry were each wrapped in cloths of blue, scarlet, or purple and covered with badgers' skins before they were put on the staves and bars.

note.label: Numbers 4: The Service of the Tabernacle Done in Order

points: Badger skin is something we would consider unclean today, yet the Lord had his holy things covered in it. Under the law of sacrifice, defilement came by touching unclean things to eat them; touching them to make something for the tabernacle still left you unclean until sundown, unable to sacrifice, but the skins themselves served the sanctuary.

note.label: Numbers 4: The Service of the Tabernacle Done in Order

points: After Aaron and his sons made an end of covering the sanctuary, the sons of Kohath came to bear it, but they shall not touch any holy thing, lest they die. The Most High is very particular about the most holy things.

The Lord referred to all the tribes together as the camp. If you are not in a camp you are out of order; people avoid camps because a camp carries a certain level of order and subjection, and they want to do their own thing, which is to sit in the midst of sin.

All twelve tribes are not gathered together right now, but we are still commanded to rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord, and that takes gathering; the body must move in one unison, in one direction, as a camp.

The burning of the sweet incense stayed in that priestly line: Zacharias, of the course of Abia, descended from the line of the Kohathites, and his lot was to burn incense in the temple of the Lord.
Luke 1:6 is the New Testament precept for what it means to be righteous: walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless. Highlight that and commit it to memory.

The son of Zacharias was John the Baptist, a Levite; and John the Baptist was Elijah back on the earth again, come to do what was prophesied of him. There is no reincarnation, coming back as a bird or such; there is regeneration, and we come back over and over again.

note.label: Numbers 4: The Service of the Tabernacle Done in Order

points: The Most High commanded that the families of the Kohathites not be cut off: Aaron and his sons appointed every one to his service and to his burden, but they shall not go in to see when the holy things are covered, lest they die.

note.label: Numbers 4: The Service of the Tabernacle Done in Order

points: The sons of Gershon were numbered from thirty to fifty years old for their service: bearing the curtains of the tabernacle, the coverings of badgers' skins, the hangings of the court and the doors, the cords, and all the instruments of their service.

note.label: Numbers 4: The Service of the Tabernacle Done in Order

points: Their charge was under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest. Ithamar had to make sure the priests had covered all the most holy things before the Gershonites came in to bear them; he was responsible for the lives of all the Gershonites that served, and he had to be in order.

note.label: Numbers 4: The Service of the Tabernacle Done in Order

points: The sons of Merari were numbered from thirty to fifty years old, charged with the boards, bars, pillars, sockets, pins, and cords of the tabernacle and the court, reckoned by name, under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron.
Only Eleazar and Ithamar were left to oversee, because Nadab and Abihu were killed by the Lord for offering strange fire; there were only two sons of Aaron remaining.

note.label: Numbers 4: The Service of the Tabernacle Done in Order

points: The Lord constantly repeats himself through these chapters to make sure you stay in order and do not go out of order, because going out of order cost your life. That is why you read the same thing in the Bible over and over again.

note.label: Numbers 4: The Service of the Tabernacle Done in Order

points: The numbered for service were 2,750 Kohathites, 2,630 Gershonites, and 3,200 Merarites; the total of those from thirty to fifty years old that entered the service of the tabernacle was 8,580, eight thousand and five hundred and fourscore.
